catalog_quote: General features of Nyesam • 23 Consonants & 6 Vowels • Implosives & labial-velar consonants. • Lexical and grammatical tone. Three tonemes (H M and L). Contour tones are a result of multiple tones assigned to one TBU. • SVO • Human vs. non human • Alienable vs. inalienable [slide 5:] Verb forms • Underived verb forms are monosyllabic and disyllabic (compositional meaning for others). • No characteristic tone melody is associated with this grammatical category. • No infinitive marker. • Citation forms are singular imperatives. [Villa 2018 SyWAL, slide 4 'General features':] 22 Consonants & 7 Vowels Lexical and grammatical tone (TBU: mora). Monosyllabic Noun and Verb stems. Canonical syllable stem shapes: CV(V), CV(V)C [Villa 2017 CALL, slide 4 'General Features of Sam':] Nasality and Vowel Length • Tones: three level (H,M, and L), and two contour tones (Rising and Falling)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nyesam is described as a tone language with three level tonemes (H, M, L), lexical and grammatical tone, mora as TBU, contour tones derived from tone crowding; stems are mostly monosyllabic CV(V)(C). The fieldworker's descriptions say nothing about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; only intonational final rise / raised H in polar questions (Villa 2018 CALL slides 5, 16)
new_statements.domain_note: Statements are inventory-level summaries on conference slides, not a phonology chapter; no word-level prominence discussed. Verb citation forms = singular imperatives.
new_statements.identity_note: Villa's slides describe Nyesam (autonym ɲé sàm, exonym Kpasham) as spoken in Kpasham, Dakli and Dem villages, Demsa LGA, Adamawa State = kpas1242 exactly. Zheltov 2016 (Glottolog's other kpas1242 ref) actually describes 'Maya', the Bali-centred cluster (Bali [bcn]), and explicitly says Kpasham may be a separate language, so it should not be used as a Kpasam source.

sources.citation: Zheltov, A. Ju. 2016. Elementy morfosintaksisa jazyka maja (adamaua, niger-kongo). In V. Vinogradov et al. (eds.), Issledovanija po jazykam Afriki 6, 81-89. Moscow: Ključ-S. (Glottolog ref 590196)
sources.note: pp. 81-82: 'Фонология и тонология майа требуют дальнейшего изучения. Можно с уверенностью зафиксировать 3 регистровых тона...' (3 register tones; contour tones' phonemic status unclear); nothing on stress. NB describes 'Maya' = the Bali-centred cluster, explicitly treating Kpasham as possibly a separate language, so it is not a description of kpas1242 proper (Glottolog assignment is loose).
